title: Form breakdown
premise: One movement, done wrong then done right, from three angles. The save-driven reel — people keep it to use later.

copy.hook: You are doing this one wrong

shots.what: The mistake, in one unmistakable frame — the rounded back, the caving knee
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Exaggerate the error slightly so it reads at phone size in half a second. Side on, locked off, subject filling two thirds of the height.

shots.what: Same movement, same angle, the error held at its worst point
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Tight on the joint that is going wrong. Hold the bottom position for three seconds — this is a still frame with a slow push, not a rep.

shots.what: Full rep, side on, the reference angle
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Tripod, phone height, perfectly perpendicular. Three clean reps so the editor can pick the best one.

shots.what: Same rep, straight on from the front
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Move the tripod, do not zoom. Same distance, same height — matching the two angles is what makes the cut between them read as deliberate.

shots.what: The detail that decides it — foot position, grip width, bar path
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Floor level if it is the feet. This is the shot that earns the save, so make it unambiguous.

shots.what: The corrected rep, full speed, from the hook's angle
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Exactly the framing of shot 1. The reel is an argument and this is its conclusion — if the framing matches, the difference is all the viewer sees.

shots.what: Back to the opening framing, corrected — the loop point
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Match shot 1 so the reel loops without a seam. A loop that lands is a second view you did not have to earn.
